Definition: contracted from a primary word; soil; by extension a region, or the solid part or the whole of the terrene globe (including the occupants in each application):--country, earth(-ly), ground, land, world.
BiblicalUsage: When Scripture says gē, it means country, earth, ground, land, world. The word appears 221 times, and in Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John it carries that same straightforward meaning. Nothing hidden sits behind it; the sense is the one you would expect from the word itself.
TheologicalSignificance: gē matters to me because the earth is the Lord’s, and every part of it belongs to Him. My position is simple: I take God at His word here, and I build on that.
RelatedEvents: The Magi Visit Jesus; The Healing of the Paralytic; The Birth of Jesus
